intent: A surveyor's brag: one line, two oceans, no wall. Numbers land like mile markers.
pacing_profile: fact-first hook at pace, three option pairs, 3-s beat, the line draws itself on the reveal, three number beats, punchline + four-word follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).

lines.direction: a number first, like a dare
lines.text: Eight thousand eight hundred and ninety-one kilometres… no wall. Where is the world's longest land border?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: Canada and the USA, Kazakhstan and Russia, or Argentina and Chile?
Canada and the USA: one line from the Atlantic to the Pacific, then Alaska to the Arctic.
Alaska alone adds two thousand four hundred and seventy-five kilometres.
Through forest, a six metre strip is kept clear so the line stays visible.
Over eight thousand monuments mark it, some only forty-six centimetres apart.

lines.direction: punchline, then four words — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Ocean to ocean, a single line. Follow for more maps.
